statement: Sealed, committed and pushed before any held-out layer's tokens are counted. Run once, on this machine. Published whichever way it lands.
claim: The format's own goal line: "COMPRESSION: max info, min tokens".
question: Does the same content cost fewer tokens as KonomiStandard than as plain JSON — and how much does a shared dictionary add, where the receiver already holds the entries?

method.twin: measure/ksjson.mjs turns each layer's notation into minified JSON by fixed rules; anything it cannot read stays a whole string, so the JSON errs SMALL (in the format's disfavour, never its favour); coverage proves every word and number survives
method.dev: layers 0, 1, 2, 3 (meta-standard, base UDTs, ISA-95, ISA-88) were used to build the twin
method.held: layers 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (ISA-101, ISA-18.2, OPC-UA, MQTT/Sparkplug, Modbus, KPIs, crosswalks) are held out; the USAGE (Python) and GOAL sections are left out
method.asWritten: the notation is measured exactly as Thomas wrote it, its ──── header rules included
method.dictionary: every block of the held-out layers is an entry with an address (ID/block, e.g. "ISA-18.2/UDT:Alarm"); the arm compares all entries sent whole against only their addresses

tokens.claude: the official claude CLI (claude-sonnet-5-5) on Simon's own login, no tools, one-word system prompt: tokens of a text = the input tokens the CLI reports for it minus those it reports for a one-character message
tokens.local: qwen2.5:7b in Ollama on this machine: the prompt tokens Ollama reports for the raw text, a one-character flush between texts so no prompt cache is shared

rules.rule: the JSON twin of every held-out layer carries every word and number of the notation (coverage at least 0.999)
with no shared dictionary, the held-out layers cost at least 1.2× more Claude tokens as JSON than as KonomiStandard
and every held-out layer costs fewer Claude tokens as KonomiStandard
with a shared dictionary, sending the addresses instead of the entries saves at least 10× in Claude tokens

disclosures: Kar read the whole spec, held-out layers included, while building the twin, and saw their character counts; no tokens of a held-out layer were counted before this seal.
The baseline is minified JSON, the leanest conventional form. Pretty-printed JSON or prose would make the format look better; this does not use them.
There is no published ISA document to compare against — the standards are paywalled — so this measures the notation as an encoding, not as a summary of the standards.

predictions.said: before any held-out layer's tokens were counted, by Kar
predictions.lossless-twin: pass — the twin keeps every word on the development layers
predictions.saves-without-dictionary: fail — the characters were within about 10% on the layers I built it on, and the ──── header rules cost tokens; I expect roughly 0.9× to 1.15×
predictions.every-layer-saves: fail — on some layers the JSON twin is already shorter in characters
predictions.dictionary-multiplies: pass — an address is a handful of tokens and an entry is tens to hundreds; I expect 10× to 25×
